area: Outside research: proven patterns and pitfalls for gamified todo/habit, exercise, autonomous effort grading, mastery tracking, frictionless capture, and ethics, mapped onto the XTNL knowledge engine
summary: The strongest external evidence points to a small set of mechanics. Grade effort from the task's own fixed properties plus measured time/intensity, never from how often the user failed it; Habitica's "red tasks pay more" exploit (GitHub issue #2639) is the cautionary case, and this app's difficulty.ts:13-18 already refuses the equivalent for Ideas. For exercise, Foster's session-RPE (RPE x minutes, r=0.75-0.90 against heart-rate methods) with a MET-minute fallback (2024 Compendium, WHO 150-300 moderate / 75-150 vigorous min per week) is the fairest cross-modality measure. Banister-style 42-day fitness / 7-day fatigue averages make honest gauges, but ACWR-style injury claims are not supported (Impellizzeri 2020). Streaks work, but they work best when repairable and forgiving. Silverman & Barasch (JCR 2023) found broken streaks reduce later engagement, and repair softens the drop. Lally 2010 found one missed day does not materially slow habit formation. Loop Habit Tracker's EWMA strength score does not reset on a miss. Duolingo freezes/repair, Apple's 90-day ring pause, Todoist's vacation mode and days off, and Habitica's Inn plus Record Yesterday's Activity all put this into practice. For recurrence, use three modes: a fixed schedule (Todoist "every" / RRULE), after-completion ("every!", TickTick "By Completion Date"), and N-per-period targets (Streaks, TickTick). The existing SRS ladder (xp.ts:206-241) is already an adaptive after-completion recurrence. For compulsory tasks, Beeminder's akrasia horizon (you can only make a goal easier a week out) and CARES commitment contracts (11% uptake, +3.4-5.7 pp 12-month quit rate) show that commitments work. They need to be bounded and self-expiring, which the app's debuff rules (debuffs.ts:12-24) already require. For autonomous grading, the planning fallacy (Buehler 1994: predicted 33.9 days, actual 55.5) argues for Spolsky-style personal calibration (estimate/actual velocity). LLM judges show position, verbosity and self-enhancement bias, so a model should output a 3-5 level anchored band that code turns into numbers, the same split gemini.ts:314-322 and mastery.ts:145-148 already use. For mastery, deliberate practice explains only 26% (games) down to under 1% (professions) of performance variance (Macnamara 2014), and Ericsson called 10,000 hours an average, not a threshold. Mastery therefore needs demonstrated outcomes (tests, PRs, challenges; the Khan Academy Attempted/Familiar/Proficient/Mastered ladder; Glicko-style uncertainty) rather than hours, which mirrors domainLevel = min(points, depth) in xp.ts:327-331. For capture, the leaders use one-line natural-language quick add (Todoist, Things), a GTD inbox that is clarified later, and share or voice entry. Todoist's Gemini-based Ramble reached only about 62% end-to-end success by Dec 2025, so a deterministic parser with a visible, undoable parse should stay the primary path. On ethics, the evidence says rewards and measurement can erode intrinsic motivation: Deci et al. 1999 found d = -0.28 to -0.40, and Etkin 2016 found quantification increases output but lowers enjoyment. Black-hat drives (loss, scarcity, unpredictability) lead to burnout, while framing rest as a bonus (WoW rested XP) and capacity caps (Sunsama) guard against it. The main codebase pitfalls I found are these. Day boundaries are inconsistent: some code uses UTC, due.ts uses the server's local time, and the deploy region is icn1. The daily streak is derived only from Idea.updatedAt, so an exercise-only day would break it. The Domain depth cap would freeze any Idea-less 'life' Domain at level 1. There is only one daily cron.

facts.topic: Habitica task value, difficulty and the red-task exploit
facts.detail: Each Habitica task has a value (colour). New tasks start yellow. Value rises toward blue on completion and falls toward red on misses or negative habits. The completion delta is 0.9747^value, with value clamped to [-47.27, 21.27] inside the formula. Difficulty multipliers are trivial 0.1, easy 1, medium 1.5, hard 2. Missed-daily damage starts at 2/3/4 HP (easy/medium/hard) and grows as the task reddens. Pitfall: XP and gold fall as value rises, so red tasks pay the most. GitHub issue #2639 (2014, still open with no maintainer fix) documents players deliberately letting tasks go red before level-ups; #3251 covers unbounded values. Sources: https://habitica.fandom.com/wiki/Difficulty , https://github.com/HabitRPG/habitica/issues/2639 , https://github.com/HabitRPG/habitica/issues/3251
facts.reuse: Do not let a task's reward rise because it was failed. Keep this app's rule (difficulty.ts:13-18; schema.prisma:206 Idea.difficulty is 'decided automatically from what the card asks', not performance) for tasks: a task's difficulty is fixed at creation and adjusted only by measured effort (minutes, RPE), never by miss history. A small set of labelled difficulty bands like Habitica's 0.1/1/1.5/2 fits the DifficultyBand pattern (difficulty.ts:38).

facts.topic: Day boundary, 'record yesterday' and pause (Habitica CDS / RYA / Inn)
facts.detail: Habitica's Custom Day Start sets when the user's day rolls over. On the first action after it, the Record Yesterday's Activity modal lists yesterday's unchecked dailies so they can be ticked before cron applies damage. 'Rest in the Inn' suspends damage for illness or vacation. Sources: https://habitica.fandom.com/wiki/Custom_Day_Start , https://habitica.fandom.com/wiki/Dailies , https://habitica.fandom.com/wiki/Rest_in_the_Inn
facts.reuse: The app has no single user-day definition today. streak.ts:31 uses date_trunc on the DB (UTC); field-streaks.ts:19-21 and mastery.ts:119-121 use UTC midnight; daily-focus.ts is a function of the UTC date; due.ts:45-49 uses the server-local setHours; due.ts:30-40 admits that true local time needs the client offset threaded through. vercel.json deploys to icn1 (Seoul), so UTC midnight falls mid-morning for the user and a 7am workout lands on 'yesterday'. Daily todos need one userDayStart (for example 04:00 local) used by all day-granular code, a 'record yesterday' confirmation before any miss is charged, and an Inn/pause flag.

facts.detail: Every completed task earns Karma. Bonus Karma comes from meeting daily/weekly goals and from goal streaks, with extra for using recurring dates, labels, filters and reminders. Karma is lost for tasks five or more days overdue. Vacation mode keeps Karma and streaks intact, and 'days off' excludes chosen weekdays from goal streaks. Sources: https://www.todoist.com/help/articles/introduction-to-karma-OgWkWy , https://www.todoist.com/help/todoist/features/turn-on-or-off-vacation-mode-in-todoist-pAQmRp
facts.reuse: The goal-bonus shape matches the existing weekly quota (field-quota.ts:7-29, sub-linear and capped at 7) and its Monday anchor (field-quota.ts:35-42). Make days-off and vacation first-class inputs to every streak and quota evaluation. The overdue penalty should be a bounded, self-expiring debuff (debuffs.ts:12-24), not a points debit.

facts.topic: Recurrence models: fixed schedule vs after-completion vs frequency target
facts.detail: Todoist: 'every Friday' is absolute; 'every! 7 days' / 'after 3 days' schedules from the actual completion. TickTick custom repeat has By Due Date, By Completion Date and By Specific Dates, and a habit streak is relative to its frequency target (for example 3x/week). The Streaks app supports specific weekdays, N days/week, N days/month and every-other-day, plus negative tasks that start checked and are unticked on a lapse. RFC 5545 RRULE is available in JS via rrule.js, whose toText()/fromText() natural-language support is incomplete. Sources: https://www.todoist.com/help/articles/complete-a-task-with-a-recurring-date-dmI6SVqdP , https://2sync.com/blog/todoist-recurring-tasks , https://help.ticktick.com/articles/7055782206349770752 , https://blog.ticktick.com/2019/06/03/habit510/ , https://thesweetsetup.com/how-to-track-your-habits-using-streaks/ , https://www.npmjs.com/package/rrule/v/2.1.0
facts.reuse: Store recurrence as {mode: FIXED(RRULE string) | AFTER_COMPLETION(N days) | TARGET(N per week/month) | ONCE}. The SRS interval ladder (xp.ts:206-241 nextIntervalDays, with grace in xp.ts:249-258) is already an adaptive after-completion recurrence, so knowledge review becomes one recurrence type in the same model. Compute today's instances lazily as a pure function of date and rule, as daily-focus.ts:15-19 does ('stored nowhere… cannot be re-rolled'), rather than by cron: vercel.json has only one daily cron, at 00:00 UTC.

facts.topic: Habit strength instead of a hard-reset streak (Loop + Lally 2010)
facts.detail: Loop Habit Tracker's score is an EWMA: S_n = (1-a)S_{n-1} + a on completion and (1-b)S_{n-1} on a miss, with a = b ≈ 0.052, calibrated so 66 consecutive completions reach about 97%. A miss lowers the score but does not reset it. Lally et al. 2010: median 66 days to 95% automaticity (range 18-254), and 'missing one opportunity to perform the behaviour did not materially affect the habit formation process'. Sources: https://github.com/iSoron/uhabits , https://www.researchgate.net/publication/32898894_How_are_habits_formed_Modeling_habit_formation_in_the_real_world
facts.reuse: field-streaks.ts:109-111 resets a streak to 1 on any gap longer than a day, and a 14+ day break applies DOUBT (field-streaks.ts:47-53; debuff-meta.ts:47-54, -8% attributes for 72h). For life habits, add an EWMA strength next to (or instead of) the counter. It suits the codebase's saturating-curve style (streakBonusPercent 2.5*sqrt(days), capped at 20%: field-streaks.ts:24-31).

facts.detail: Silverman & Barasch, JCR 49(6) 2023, seven studies: highlighting intact rather than broken streaks increases later engagement regardless of actual behaviour. The effect is amplified when the user blames themselves for the break and attenuated when the streak can be repaired. Duolingo: a streak freeze fills a missed day. Allowing two equipped freezes reportedly raised DAU by 0.38%; streak repair within about 48h and the weekend amulet exist. Former CPO Mazal says freezes were added 'so no one feels like they failed if they miss a day' (the 0.38% figure comes from secondary analyses). Apple watchOS 11 adds per-weekday ring goals and lets you pause rings for up to 90 days without breaking the streak. Sources: https://academic.oup.com/jcr/article-abstract/49/6/1095/6623414 , https://www.lennysnewsletter.com/p/how-duolingo-reignited-user-growth , https://duolingo.deconstructoroffun.com/mechanics/streaks , https://blog.duolingo.com/protecting-streaks-from-site-issues/ , https://support.apple.com/guide/watch/adjust-your-activity-ring-goals-apd29b30023c/watchos , https://www.macrumors.com/2024/06/18/watchos-11-custom-activity-goals-different-days/
facts.reuse: Freezes must be earned deterministically (for example one per 7 active days, holding at most 2), never drawn at random, to respect README:518-525. Add a repair window (a make-up task within 48h) and planned rest days. Keep the existing kindness rule that a penalty lands on return, not while away (field-streaks.ts:77-81). The home daily streak (streak.ts:15-24) is derived only from Idea.updatedAt, so it will break on a day with only workouts or todos unless those events feed it.

facts.detail: Polivy & Herman (dieting research, 1970s onward): after a perceived rule violation, people abandon the rule entirely. It is the belief of having failed, not the violation itself, that triggers the spiral. The effect generalises to exercise, study and work goals. Sources: https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/psychology/abstinence-violation , https://en.wikiversity.org/wiki/Motivation_and_emotion/Book/2021/What_the_hell_effect
facts.reuse: The day after a missed compulsory task should offer a cheap way back (a minimum viable version, a repair quest), not an escalating penalty. Frame misses as recoverable, in line with debuffs.ts:12-24 ('never destructive… always self-expiring').

facts.topic: Compulsory tasks as commitment devices (Beeminder, CARES)
facts.detail: Beeminder: you 'derail' when you end a day on the wrong side of the red line. Pledges escalate $5, $10, $30, $90, $270, $810. Making a goal easier only takes effect after about a week (the 'akrasia horizon'), which blocks last-minute wriggling. CARES (Giné, Karlan, Zinman 2010): 11% of smokers took up the commitment account; those offered it were 3.4-5.7 pp more likely to pass a surprise 12-month test. Sources: https://doc.beeminder.com/jargon , https://blog.beeminder.com/exponential/ , https://www.aeaweb.org/articles?id=10.1257%2Fapp.2.4.213
facts.reuse: 'Compulsory' = a committed flag plus an akrasia horizon: downgrading, deleting or rescheduling a compulsory task takes effect in 7 days unless a reason is logged. Stakes should be in-game only: a bounded debuff kind or a negative ledger row with a free-string reason (MasteryLedgerEntry.reason, schema.prisma:334-351, needs no migration). Escalate the Beeminder way but cap it, as debuff-meta.ts:22-24 does with maxMagnitude. Never real money. Uptake data shows opt-in commitment matters.

facts.topic: Goal tiers: committed vs aspirational OKR grading
facts.detail: Google re:Work grades OKRs from 0.0 to 1.0. Committed OKRs are expected to score 1.0 and a miss needs explaining; aspirational OKRs are expected to average 0.6-0.7 with high variance. Sources: https://rework.withgoogle.com/intl/en/guides/set-goals-with-okrs , https://www.whatmatters.com/okrs-explained/grading-okrs
facts.reuse: Map the user's short/mid/long goals: short goals and compulsory tasks are committed (binary, 1.0 expected); mid and long goals are aspirational, graded 0-1 against measurable key results, with 0.7 counting as success. An aspirational miss should never trigger a debuff.

facts.topic: Goal-pursuit science: implementation intentions, goal gradient, fresh start
facts.detail: Gollwitzer & Sheeran 2006: if-then plans, d = 0.65 (95% CI 0.6-0.7) across roughly 94 studies. Kivetz, Urminsky & Zheng 2006: people speed up about 20% near a reward. A 12-stamp card with 2 free stamps was completed in a median 10 days versus 15 for a plain 10-stamp card. Dai, Milkman & Riis 2014: aspirational behaviour rises after temporal landmarks, with gym visits up 33% at a new week and 47% at a new semester. Sources: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/37367696_Implementation_Intentions_and_Goal_Achievement_A_Meta-Analysis_of_Effects_and_Processes , https://journals.sagepub.com/doi/abs/10.1509/jmkr.43.1.39 , https://pubsonline.informs.org/doi/10.1287/mnsc.2014.1901
facts.reuse: Add an optional 'when/where' slot to capture (never required). Goal progress bars must be real, since the README refuses fabricated progress (README:479-488, 541-546), so no free 'pre-stamps'; use honest bars like domainLevelProgress (xp.ts:345-361). Schedule goal reviews and weekly resets on landmarks (Monday, already the week anchor in field-quota.ts:35-42; month start).

facts.detail: Load (arbitrary units) = session RPE on the CR-10 scale x duration in minutes. Individual correlations with summed heart-rate-zone load are r = 0.75-0.90, and a meta-analysis supports criterion validity. It is less precise than objective measures. RPE should be collected about 15-30 minutes after the session. Sources: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4213373/ , https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s13102-023-00712-5 , https://www.researchgate.net/publication/11645805_A_New_Approach_to_Monitoring_Exercise_Training
facts.reuse: Use this as the base of deterministic exercise grading: xp = f(RPE x minutes), comparable across lifting, running and climbing. Clamp inputs server-side as xp.ts:89-95 clamps the client-sent combo. Prompt for RPE after the session, not at the start.

facts.topic: Fitness/fatigue modelling and the ACWR warning
facts.detail: Banister impulse-response model: every session adds a slowly decaying fitness impulse (about 42 days) and a fast fatigue impulse (about 7 days). TrainingPeaks' CTL (42-day EWMA), ATL (7-day EWMA) and TSB = CTL - ATL implement it. Strava Relative Effort weights time in heart-rate zones and shows a weekly range from a 3-week moving average. Impellizzeri et al. 2020 found no evidence that the acute:chronic workload ratio reduces injury risk and identified statistical coupling problems. Sources: https://www.trainingpeaks.com/learn/articles/the-science-of-the-performance-manager/ , https://support.strava.com/en-us/articles/15401794-relative-effort , https://medium.com/strava-engineering/quantifying-effort-through-heart-rate-data-e6a0e3dd6a52 , https://journals.humankinetics.com/view/journals/ijspp/15/6/article-p907.xml
facts.reuse: Show 42-day and 7-day EWMA gauges of session-RPE load as honest 'Fitness' and 'Fatigue' bars, measured and null when history is thin, as progress-rate.ts:10-18 does. Apply diminishing XP above the user's 3-week weekly range (a burnout guard) and reuse FATIGUED (debuff-meta.ts:38-45). Do not present any ratio as an injury predictor.

facts.topic: MET-minutes and WHO thresholds for fair cross-activity scoring
facts.detail: The 2024 Adult Compendium lists 1,114 activities (303 new), 82% with measured METs. Light is 1.6-2.9 METs, moderate 3.0-5.9, vigorous 6.0 and above. WHO 2020 recommends that adults get 150-300 minutes of moderate or 75-150 minutes of vigorous activity per week, plus muscle-strengthening on at least 2 days. Sources: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/38242596/ , https://pacompendium.com/ , https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC7719906/
facts.reuse: When no RPE is given, fall back to MET x minutes from a small built-in activity table. Weekly exercise thresholds (vigorous minutes counted double toward 150, plus 2 strength days) come from the literature, which meets the README's demand for levels that mean something (xp.ts:269-282). The existing lexicon already routes fitness words to PHYSICAL (attribute-inference.ts:134), and an exercise log would be the honest source for PHYSICAL, which currently comes only from studying fitness text (attributes.ts:3-11).

facts.detail: Zourdos 2016 RIR-based RPE: RPE 10 = 0 reps in reserve, validated against bar velocity (r = -0.88 in experienced lifters, -0.77 in novices); experienced lifters are more accurate. Epley e1RM = w x (1 + reps/30), about ±5% for 2-10 reps. Double progression adds reps to the top of a range, then adds the smallest load increment. Strava Best Efforts auto-detects the top 3 lifetime and top 10 annual efforts per distance, and PR medals apply only from the second attempt. Sources: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26049792/ , https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/One-repetition_maximum , https://legionathletics.com/double-progression/ , https://support.strava.com/hc/en-us/articles/16601494390285-Best-Efforts
facts.reuse: Treat PRs (e1RM per lift, best pace per distance, longest session) as deterministic one-time milestone events, like MASTERY_BONUS (xp.ts:62-68) and IDEA_MASTERED in the ledger (mastery.ts:85-89). Reward progression achievements more than raw volume. Suggest the next double-progression target as a generated task.

facts.topic: Narrative and bundling for exercise (Zombies, Run!, temptation bundling)
facts.detail: Zombies, Run!: story missions with audio between music tracks; supplies are auto-collected while running, with no phone interaction, and later fund a base-building meta-game. Milkman, Minson & Volpp 2014 (n=226): gym-only access to page-turner audiobooks gave 51% more gym visits at first, fading after the Thanksgiving break; 61% later paid for gym-only access. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zombies,_Run! , https://blog.zombiesrungame.com/2022/03/30/ten-years-of-zombies-run/ , https://ideas.repec.org/a/inm/ormnsc/v60y2014i2p283-299.html
facts.reuse: The Arcane Terminal RPG layer (bosses, boons, emblems) can wrap a workout as a mission. Rewards should be credited after the session with no mid-workout UI. Effects fade after routine breaks, so re-engagement after a gap should offer something new rather than a penalty.

facts.topic: Overjustification and the cost of quantification
facts.detail: Deci, Koestner & Ryan 1999 (128 studies): engagement-contingent, completion-contingent and performance-contingent rewards undermined free-choice intrinsic motivation (d = -0.40, -0.36, -0.28), as did all tangible and expected rewards. Etkin 2016 (JCR best article): measuring everyday activities (walking, reading) increases how much people do but decreases enjoyment, continued engagement and well-being. Sources: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/10589297 , https://academic.oup.com/jcr/article-abstract/42/6/967/2358309
facts.reuse: Let a task be marked 'intrinsic' or 'play': it is logged with informational feedback only (a PR, competence, time) and no XP payout. Prefer competence feedback over engagement-contingent points for activities the user already enjoys.

facts.detail: Strathern (1997): 'When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure.' Campbell: the more a quantitative indicator is used for decisions, the more it is subject to corruption pressures. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodhart's_law , https://rss.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1111/j.1740-9713.2018.01205.x
facts.reuse: The app already defends against this for knowledge. domainLevel = min(pointsLevel, depth) (xp.ts:318-331) stops volume-only levels; yieldXp decays e^(-λ·N_similar) for near-duplicates (xp.ts:157-168); review mastery is 'negligible per click' (mastery.ts:43-61). Apply the same to tasks: similarity decay on near-identical task titles (reuse embeddings and dedup bands, xp.ts:388-434) to stop one chore being split into ten, a sqrt soft cap on daily task XP, and outcome gates (a goal completed, a PR) on level-ups.

facts.topic: Estimation calibration (planning fallacy, Evidence-Based Scheduling, Sunsama)
facts.detail: Buehler, Griffin & Ross 1994: students predicted 33.9 days for a thesis and took 55.5, worse than their own worst-case estimate of 48.6; only about 30% finished on time. Spolsky's Evidence-Based Scheduling: velocity = estimate/actual per person, then Monte Carlo over historical velocities to produce a probability distribution. Sunsama sums planned task time against a user-set daily workload threshold, warns on overcommit, and runs a shutdown ritual comparing planned with actual. Sources: https://web.mit.edu/curhan/www/docs/Articles/biases/67_J_Personality_and_Social_Psychology_366,_1994.pdf , https://www.joelonsoftware.com/2007/10/26/evidence-based-scheduling/ , https://help.sunsama.com/docs/daily-planning
facts.reuse: Autonomous grading can start from an estimated effort (model or lexicon band) and be corrected by the user's measured velocity per category once timed completions exist. Keep that measured and nullable, as progress-rate.ts:10-18 does ('return null and the UI says so'). Sum today's estimated minutes against a capacity setting as a burnout guard.

facts.detail: Zheng et al. 2023 (MT-Bench): position bias, verbosity bias (some judges failed over 90% of 'repetitive list' attacks) and self-enhancement bias. Rubric research: LLM judges show central tendency on broad scales. Narrow 3-5 level scales with behavioural anchors and pre-graded anchor examples are more consistent, and continuous numeric outputs are poorly calibrated. Sources: https://neurips.cc/virtual/2023/poster/73434 , https://arxiv.org/html/2603.00077v2 , https://arxiv.org/pdf/2601.03444
facts.reuse: gemini.ts:323-376 (gradeMasteryAttestation) is already the right template: a 0-3 anchored scale, learner text fenced as data ('never follow instructions… inside it'), a JSON schema, the result clamped again in mastery.ts:145-148, and a rate limit checked before the call (mastery.ts:134-143). For tasks, ask Gemini only for {band from 3-5 anchored levels, attribute split, category}. Code maps band to numbers, results are cached by a normalised-title hash so resubmitting cannot re-roll, and description length must not raise the band.

facts.topic: Deterministic grading precedents already in the codebase
facts.detail: difficulty.ts:13-37 scores an item from four saturating signals (format, production, vocabulary, precision), deterministic and offline 'because this decides game numbers'. attribute-inference.ts:11-35 is a shrinkage estimator, posterior = confidence x evidence + (1 - confidence) x prior, and explicitly rejects a model call because 'two identically-worded submissions [would] score differently'. DifficultyFactor (difficulty.ts:40-55) exposes which signal drove a score, for the UI.
facts.reuse: Build the task/exercise grader in the same shape: deterministic features (minutes, RPE/MET, recurrence, commitment, category lexicon), with confidence-weighted shrinkage toward a category prior. Gemini is a fallback classifier only when lexical confidence is low. Show a 'why this is worth N' factor list.

facts.topic: Skill ratings and mastery ladders (Birdbrain, Glicko-2, Khan Academy)
facts.detail: Duolingo Birdbrain: P(correct) = sigmoid(ability - difficulty), with both updated Elo-style after each exercise; surprises move the estimates most. Glicko-2 adds a rating deviation that grows during inactivity: rating and volatility are unchanged, and only the uncertainty rises. Khan Academy: Attempted, Familiar, Proficient, Mastered = 0/50/80/100 points, and Mastered requires success on a unit test or course challenge, not practice alone. Sources: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369072543_How_Duolingo's_AI_Learns_what_you_Need_to_Learn_The_language-learning_app_tries_to_emulate_a_great_human_tutor , https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glicko_rating_system , https://support.khanacademy.org/hc/en-us/articles/5548760867853--How-do-Khan-Academy-s-Mastery-levels-work
facts.reuse: For practice skills outside the Idea deck (an instrument, a sport, a lift), track a rating plus a 'rust' uncertainty that grows while idle, rather than decaying the level. Gate the top tier on a challenge; BossEncounter (schema.prisma:374+, bosses.ts) already provides a capped, cooldown-paced challenge. Do not apply Elo difficulty to Ideas: difficulty.ts:13-18 deliberately keeps Idea difficulty independent of performance.

facts.detail: Macnamara, Hambrick & Oswald 2014: deliberate practice explained 26% of performance variance in games, 21% in music, 18% in sports, 4% in education and under 1% in professions. Ericsson (Peak; Salon 2016): 10,000 hours was an average for elite violinists, not a threshold; the kind and quality of practice matter more than volume. Sources: https://gwern.net/doc/psychology/2014-macnamara.pdf , https://www.salon.com/2016/04/10/malcolm_gladwell_got_us_wrong_our_research_was_key_to_the_10000_hour_rule_but_heres_what_got_oversimplified/
facts.reuse: Hours can be one input to mastery tracking but never the level itself. Mirror domainLevel's two-axis cap (xp.ts:318-331): level = min(effort-based level, demonstrated-outcome level), where outcomes are PRs, passed challenges, goal completions or attestations (mastery.ts:123-156). Display hours as context, not as rank.

facts.detail: Todoist Quick Add parses natural-language dates and recurrences ('every other Tuesday starting March 3'), {deadline}, p1-p3 and labels, and a misparsed word can be tapped back to plain text. Todoist Ramble (GA 21 Jan 2026, Gemini 2.5 Flash Live) turns speech into structured tasks, but end-to-end success only rose from ~40% (Oct 2025) to ~62% (Dec 2025). Things Quick Entry with Autofill is a global shortcut that grabs the current link or email. GTD: capture everything into one inbox now, clarify later, do anything under 2 minutes immediately, and run a weekly review. The Web Share Target API (manifest share_target) makes an installed PWA/TWA a share destination on Android. chrono-node parses NL dates in JS. Sources: https://www.todoist.com/help/articles/use-task-quick-add-in-todoist-va4Lhpzz , https://www.todoist.com/help/articles/dictate-to-add-tasks-with-ramble-P1Raq7vVF , https://culturedcode.com/things/support/articles/2249437/ , https://asana.com/resources/getting-things-done-gtd , https://developer.chrome.com/docs/android/trusted-web-activity/web-share-target , https://github.com/wanasit/chrono
facts.reuse: manifest.ts:31-34 already declares app shortcuts (Review, Add), and manifest.ts:5-6 notes a TWA Android wrapper, so add a 'Quick task' and 'Log workout' shortcut and a share_target. Use a single-line capture box with deterministic parsing (chrono-node + rrule + prefixes such as '!' compulsory, '~30m', 'rpe7', '#goal') and zero required fields. Save first, grade asynchronously, and show the parse as editable chips. The Add form's autocorrect and word-complete (autocorrect.ts:1-20, WordComplete.tsx) can be reused for titles.

facts.detail: Zagal, Björk & Lewis 2013 (FDG) set out dark patterns in games: temporal (grinding, playing by appointment), monetary and social-capital based. Octalysis: black-hat drives (scarcity, unpredictability, loss avoidance) drive short-term engagement but lead to burnout; white-hat drives (meaning, accomplishment, empowerment) sustain. Eyal's Manipulation Matrix: a maker who uses the product and whose product materially improves lives is a 'facilitator', though critics note that is necessary, not sufficient. Hamari et al. 2014: 24 empirical studies, mostly positive but strongly context-dependent. SuperBetter RCT (Roepke 2015, n=283): the gamified app beat a waitlist on depressive symptoms. Finch uses no penalties for missed days. Sources: https://deceptive.design/articles/dark-patterns-in-the-design-of-games/ , https://yukaichou.com/gamification-study/white-hat-black-hat-gamification-octalysis-framework/ , https://designli.co/blog/using-the-manipulation-matrix-for-ethical-behavioral-design/ , https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1109/hicss.2014.377 , https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/26182069/ , https://www.internetmatters.org/advice/apps-and-platforms/wellbeing/finch/
facts.reuse: README:507-535 already refuses a variable-ratio streak claim, loss-aversion copy and fabricated axes. xp.ts:106-155 allows only bounded variance with expected value 1.0 and a published band. Carry the same line into life systems: no appointment mechanics beyond the user's own schedule, no guilt notifications (notifications.ts:26-31 is a derived, read-only feed, which is a good model), and loss framing kept to bounded debuffs.

facts.detail: WoW rested XP gives 200% kill XP after logging off, earning one 'bubble' (5% of a level) per 8 hours rested. Players hated the same numbers when presented as a penalty for long play and liked them as a bonus for resting. Sunsama has a workload threshold and overcommit warnings. Apple offers ring pause and per-weekday goals; Todoist offers days off and vacation mode. Fogg's B=MAP and Tiny Habits: behaviour needs motivation, ability and a prompt together, and the recipe 'After I [anchor], I will [tiny behaviour], then celebrate' keeps the minimum under 30 seconds. Sources: https://www.psychologyofgames.com/2010/03/framing-and-world-of-warcrafts-rest-system/ , https://wowpedia.fandom.com/wiki/Rest , https://help.sunsama.com/docs/daily-planning , https://www.behaviormodel.org/
facts.reuse: Replace 'penalty for absence' with 'rested bonus after declared rest days' where possible. Add a daily capacity check on scheduled task minutes. Give each compulsory task a 'minimum viable version' that keeps the streak alive at reduced XP. The existing diminishing combo shape (mastery.ts:63-82, sqrt capped at +50%) is a ready template for a daily task-XP soft cap.

facts.topic: Existing economy scale the new systems must fit into
facts.detail: Review payout: 2 x (1 + 0.18 x (level - 1)) x combo (xp.ts:42-104), plus bounded ±12% variance (xp.ts:131-155). New-idea yield: 10-40 base (xp.ts:14-23) decayed by similarity. Mastery points: 0.1 x level per review (mastery.ts:57-61), 25 per mastered Idea (mastery.ts:39), attestations 0-3 once per UTC day (mastery.ts:40, 128-156); the tree is priced so reaching an Ultimate is 'a campaign measured in real months' (mastery.ts:26-31). Idle mastery decays 5% per day, but only when something affordable is left unbought (mastery.ts:162-232). Ledgers are append-only with free-string reasons (schema.prisma:325-351, 493-503).
facts.reuse: Raw session-RPE load (a 60-minute RPE-7 session = 420 AU) or MET-minutes cannot be minted 1:1 without swamping the knowledge economy. Route life XP into its own track or attribute feed, and mint mastery points only at outcome milestones (goal completed, PR, compulsory week kept), recorded as new ledger reasons. Re-run the existing balance check (the 'balance:horizon' script referenced at mastery.ts:37) before shipping.

facts.topic: Structural traps when bolting life systems onto Fields/Domains
facts.detail: Domain level = min(pointsLevel, DEPTH_GRACE (1) + floor(sum over Ideas of (level/12)^2)) (xp.ts:316-331). Attribute scores derive only from Field levels weighted by composition (attributes.ts:3-11; skill-effects.ts:171-174). The home daily streak comes from Idea.updatedAt with no activity-log table (streak.ts:15-24; README:470-478). The debuff and boon machinery is generic and user-keyed (debuffs.ts, boons.ts; the boon draw is uniform and fires only on boss victory, bosses.ts:396).
facts.reuse: An 'Exercise' or 'Todo' Field/Domain holding no Ideas would stay at level 1 forever because of the depth cap. Life systems need their own depth signal (habit strength, PR count, goal completions), or an explicit composition path into attributes. An append-only activity/event table (the pattern MasteryLedgerEntry uses) would let streak.ts, progress-rate.ts and attributes read every kind of real activity, not just Idea edits.

constraints: No variable-ratio rewards: README:507-535 refuses the randomized streak claim and loot drop. Only a bounded size variance (±12%, EV 1.0, band published) is allowed (xp.ts:106-155). Freezes, boons and bonuses for tasks or exercise must be earned deterministically.

Debuffs must be never random, never destructive to the knowledge base, bounded by maxMagnitude and self-expiring (debuffs.ts:12-24; debuff-meta.ts:14-24). Compulsory-task consequences must fit this, and a debuff lands on return rather than while the user is away (field-streaks.ts:77-81).

Game numbers are deterministic and offline. A model judges only the user's prose and never sets rules (gemini.ts:314-322; attribute-inference.ts:31-35; difficulty.ts:35-37). Model output is clamped in code (mastery.ts:145-148) and rate-limited before the call (mastery.ts:134-143).
Difficulty is a property of the item, never of performance history (difficulty.ts:13-18; schema.prisma:206). Do not repeat Habitica's red-task exploit.

No fabricated progress or projections: README:479-488 and 541-546; progress-rate.ts:10-18 returns null when history is insufficient. Honest gauges only, and no injury-prediction claims from ACWR-style ratios (Impellizzeri 2020).
Economies are append-only ledgers with free-string reason codes (schema.prisma:325-351, 493-503), so a new income or expense source needs no migration. Keep balances as the sum of deltas.
Schema changes need hand-authored migrations applied with prisma db execute + migrate resolve --applied (README:550-555). Dev and production share one database, so no destructive experiments.
Single user (DEFAULT_USER_ID); most tables are not user-scoped (README:631).

Day boundaries are inconsistent today: UTC in streak.ts:31, field-streaks.ts:19-21, mastery.ts:119-121 and daily-focus.ts, but server-local in due.ts:45-49 (acknowledged at due.ts:30-40). The deploy region is icn1 (vercel.json). Daily todos need one user-local day start before streaks or compulsory misses are charged.
Only one Vercel cron, daily at 00:00 UTC (vercel.json). Prefer lazily derived state (daily-focus.ts:15-19; notifications.ts:26-31) for recurrence instances and miss detection.
Client-originated numbers (minutes, RPE, reps, combo) must be clamped server-side, as xp.ts:89-95 does for combo.
The mastery economy is deliberately slow and balanced by measurement (mastery.ts:26-39). Life XP must not mint mastery points at volume.
The Domain depth cap (xp.ts:327-331) keeps any Idea-less Domain at level 1. The daily streak reads only Idea.updatedAt (streak.ts:15-24), so an exercise-only day breaks it unless new events feed it.

Evidence rules: deliberate-practice hours explain little variance outside games, music and sports (Macnamara 2014), so hours must not equal mastery. Rewards and measurement can reduce intrinsic motivation (Deci 1999; Etkin 2016).
opportunities: Unified append-only ActivityEvent/LifeLedger (kind: REVIEW | TASK_DONE | WORKOUT | GOAL_KR | MISS; minutes; rpe; band; xp; attribute split), modelled on MasteryLedgerEntry. It would feed streak.ts, progress-rate.ts and attribute scores from all real activity, not just Idea.updatedAt.

One Task model covering all recurrences: {ONCE | FIXED RRULE | AFTER_COMPLETION N days | TARGET N per week/month}, tier {DAILY, SHORT, MID, LONG goal via parentId}, committed flag, optional when/where. Knowledge review becomes one auto-generated daily ('clear due cards'), with the SRS ladder (xp.ts:206-241) acting as its own after-completion recurrence.

Exercise grading: xp from session-RPE (RPE x min) with MET x minutes as a fallback, clamped. Weekly ring from WHO minimums (150 moderate-equivalent, vigorous counted double, 2 strength days). 42-day and 7-day EWMA Fitness/Fatigue gauges. Diminishing XP above the 3-week weekly range, plus FATIGUED. Auto-detected PRs (Epley e1RM, best efforts) as one-time milestones.

Autonomous grader pipeline: deterministic features, then a shrinkage estimate toward a category prior, then a band from 3-5 anchored levels, then numbers in code. Gemini is used only when lexical confidence is low (same fencing and clamp pattern as gradeMasteryAttestation), with the grade cached by a normalised-title hash. Personal calibration comes from estimate/actual velocity (EBS) once timed completions exist, and a 'why' factor list is shown as in difficulty.ts DifficultyFactor.

Anti-gaming pack: embedding-similarity decay on near-duplicate task titles (reuse yieldXp e^(-λN) and the dedup bands), a sqrt daily soft cap on task XP, outcome-gated level-ups (goal KR hit, PR, compulsory week kept), and mastery points minted only at milestones.

Habit strength (Loop EWMA, a ≈ 0.052) next to streak counts. Earned freezes (1 per 7 active days, max 2), a 48h repair quest, planned rest days, vacation/Inn mode, a custom day start, and a 'record yesterday' screen before any miss is charged.

Compulsory tasks as Beeminder-style commitments: an akrasia horizon (weakening or deleting takes effect in 7 days unless a reason is logged), escalating but capped in-game stakes via a new bounded debuff kind or ledger reason, a minimum viable version that preserves the streak, and a recovery bonus after a miss to counter the what-the-hell effect.

Goal tiers graded OKR-style: short goals committed (1.0 expected), mid and long goals aspirational (0.7 = success, no debuff). Reviews happen on fresh-start landmarks (Monday, the existing week anchor; month start), with a GTD-style weekly review screen that also clears the capture inbox.

Mastery tracking for practice skills: a Glicko-like rating plus a 'rust' uncertainty that grows while idle. A Khan-style ladder (Attempted/Familiar/Proficient/Mastered) where the top tier requires a Boss challenge (reuse BossEncounter). Level = min(effort level, demonstrated-outcome level), mirroring domainLevel.

Frictionless capture: a one-line quick-add parsed deterministically (chrono-node + rrule + prefixes '!', '~30m', 'rpe7', '#goal') and shown as editable chips. Zero required fields, save-then-grade asynchronously, manifest shortcuts ('Quick task', 'Log workout') plus Web Share Target on the existing TWA, and optional voice. Keep a deterministic path because Todoist's LLM voice capture only reached ~62% success.

Burnout guards: a daily capacity check on scheduled minutes (Sunsama), a WoW-style rested bonus after declared rest days instead of absence penalties, per-weekday targets, and a pause mode (Apple, up to 90 days).
An intrinsic/'play' tag: logged with informational feedback only (PRs, time, competence) and no XP, to avoid overjustification (Deci 1999; Etkin 2016).

Attribute integration: exercise events feed PHYSICAL and compulsory or discipline tasks feed STUBBORNNESS/SELF_RESPECT, through the existing lexicon/shrinkage estimator (attribute-inference.ts:134, :138). This gives the attribute radar a real-life substrate instead of only study text.
